YAML serialization from a bincode-like AST with base58 encoding for hashes and signatures.

# Purpose
`fd_flamenco_yaml.c` implements a YAML writer for a `bincode`-like abstract syntax tree. It defines the `fd_flamenco_yaml_t` object, with [`fd_flamenco_yaml_new`](<#fd_flamenco_yaml_new>), [`fd_flamenco_yaml_init`](<#fd_flamenco_yaml_init>), [`fd_flamenco_yaml_delete`](<#fd_flamenco_yaml_delete>), and [`fd_flamenco_yaml_file`](<#fd_flamenco_yaml_file>) for object setup and access to the output stream. The main entry point is [`fd_flamenco_yaml_walk`](<#fd_flamenco_yaml_walk>), which serializes nodes by tracking collection state, indent level, and line layout so it can print maps, arrays, options, and scalar values in YAML form.

The file handles many Flamenco value types, including integers, floating-point values, booleans, null, C strings, hashes, and signatures. It also uses Base58 encoding for hash and signature output, and it skips enum discriminator nodes during the walk. At the end of the file, [`fd_get_types_yaml`](<#fd_get_types_yaml>) creates and stores a global YAML writer that targets `stdout`, and [`fd_flush_yaml_dump`](<#fd_flush_yaml_dump>) flushes that output stream.
